$comment: Catala rule test inputs for IntestacyCascade per TT-531. AEA 1925 s.46 intestacy cascade + s.46(2A)/LPA 1925 s.184 commorientes. Scope Distribute returns ComputedOrNeedsHuman.Verdict (money) PLUS a per-member money list (per_member_amounts) — the per-heir allocation authority lives in code-inherit-test-suite/tests/oracles/intestacy-cascade-aea1925.oracle.json (T032 per-heir gov-oracle harness, TT-463 pattern), which these fixtures mirror 1:1 (same inputs, same expected per-member split). This twin is a human-readable record, NOT gate-exercised (no Makefile target consumes *.test-fixtures.json, mirroring the CatInheritanceCharge/TT-682 precedent). The oracle's locked wrong_split anti-hack negative case is deliberately NOT mirrored here — it is not a real answer and its home is the oracle file alone.

positive.decidability_claim: DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(i) Table Case (2): spouse takes chattels (£0) + fixed net sum (£322,000) + half residue (£189,000) = £511,000; issue take the other half (£189,000) per stirpes over two single-child branches = £94,500 each.
DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(i) Table Case (1): no issue -> spouse takes the whole estate absolutely (post-ITPA-2014). £20,000 chattels + £500,000 = £520,000.

DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(ii) + s.47: issue but no spouse, whole estate on the statutory trusts per stirpes. £900,000 over branches [1;1;2] -> £300,000/branch; the two-grandchild branch splits £150,000 each.
DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(iii): no spouse, no issue, both parents -> father and mother in equal shares absolutely. £400,000 / 2 = £200,000 each.
DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(v) First class: no spouse, no issue, no parent -> whole-blood siblings on the statutory trusts. £300,000 over three living siblings = £100,000 each.

edge.decidability_claim: DECIDABLE; AEA 1925 s.46(2A): spouse survived but died within the 28-day period, so treated as not having survived -> distributed as if there were no spouse (s.46(1)(ii)). £700,000 per stirpes over two single-child branches = £350,000 each. The 27/28-day boundary itself is proven by the in-file #[test] scopes on Survivorship, not by this fixture (which only exercises the boolean flip).
DECIDABLE; the £322,000 fixed net sum clamps to the £200,000 estate — spouse takes the whole (smaller) estate, issue take nothing. Proves the legacy does not over-distribute beyond the estate.

DECIDABLE; chattels are a distinct category only under s.46(1)(i)(A) (spouse takes); with no spouse, chattels remain part of the residuary estate. £300,000 + £60,000 = £360,000 over two single-child branches = £180,000 each.
NOT DECIDABLE BY RULE; AEA 1925 s.46(1)(vi) default: Crown/Duchy of Lancaster/Duke of Cornwall bona vacantia — discretionary Treasury Solicitor territory, never a computed split.
